title: Private deployments: VPC & on-prem deployment reference, day-2 ops, upgrade and rollback, and customer requirements library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments covering VPC-based hosted-control-plane deployments and fully on-prem packaging. It includes reference architectures, pre-deployment and customer requirements, on-prem packaging expectations, day-2 operations guidance, and prescriptive upgrade and rollback procedures. The goal is to provide operators, solutions engineers, and customer SREs with a single, actionable reference during deployment and production operations.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Deployment engineers, customer platform SREs, solutions engineers, and Redwood's customer success engineers.
- Scope: VPC-hosted private control plane, VPC-only model-serving in customer account, and air-gapped on-prem installations for regulated customers.
- Not covered: internal hosted API operations and Dedicated fleet internals (see separate runtime docs).

High-level deployment topologies (summary):
1) Control plane in Redwood-managed VPC, data plane in customer VPC (recommended for most enterprise customers).
2) Fully customer-hosted VPC (control + data in customer-controlled cloud account).
3) On-prem / air-gapped deployment using the on-prem packaging (for FISMA/PCI/regulated deployments).

Pre-requisites (customer and Redwood responsibilities):
- Network and connectivity:
  - Customer to provide VPC with dedicated subnets for control-plane and data-plane (minimum /24 per subnet recommended).
  - Required ports: 443 (HTTPS), 2379 (etcd, if using customer-managed etcd), 10250 (kubelet), 22 (SSH for nodes; optional if using bastion).
  - Peering / Transit: VPC peering or Transit Gateway established between Redwood control plane and customer's VPC where applicable. NAT/egress rules must allow outbound to S3-compatible storage and Redwood managed endpoints.
- Identity & secrets:
  - KMS key ARN (customer-managed) for envelope encryption of secrets is required for restricted deployments.
  - TLS certificates: Customer may provide SAN certificates for internal endpoints or accept Redwood-managed certs where allowed.
- Compute & storage:
  - GPU nodes: types and count as specified in sizing worksheet (see Customer Requirements table).
  - Persistent storage: recommend using encrypted block volumes with IOPS guarantees for model cache and KV stores.
- Compliance & access:
  - RBAC roles and user list for initial admin/ops access.
  - Audit log forwarding to customer SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) must be configured pre-deployment.

Reference architectures (textual diagrams + notes):
- Reference: Control plane (Redwood-managed) + Data plane (Customer VPC)
  - Logical components: Redwood control plane (API, scheduler, monitoring collection endpoints), customer data plane (serving pods, node pool, model cache), secure tunnel (mTLS / VPC peering).
  - Notes: Use private link or transit gateway where possible to avoid public internet transit. Configure route tables to ensure control plane can reach node-level telemetry endpoints.

- Reference: Fully customer-hosted (customer-managed control + data)
  - Logical components: Internal control plane (operator-managed), private artifact registry, operator-managed etcd (HA), load balancers in private subnets, internal ingress with strict ACLs.
  - Notes: Requires stronger operations maturity from customer (etcd backups, operator lifecycle). Redwood provides deployment manifests and an operator image set.

- Reference: Air-gapped on-prem installation
  - Logical components: On-prem orchestration (k3s/k8s), local artifact registry (harbor/nexus), model cache on NFS or block storage, HSM/KMS integration for keys, optional hardware security modules.
  - Notes: Use the air-gap packaging (tarball + signed manifests) and the offline installer. Ensure time sync (NTP) and local CA to validate signed images.

On-prem packaging and install artifacts:
- Packaging types:
  - Helm charts for supported k8s versions (recommended for customer-hosted cloud VPC).
  - Operator images + YAML manifests for customers preferring GitOps.
  - Air-gap tarball: includes container images (OCI layout), Helm charts, and verified manifest signatures.
- Install artifacts checklist:
  - Signed release manifest SHA256 and GPG signature.
  - Image digests for every component (operator, runtime, sidecars, metrics collector).
  - values.yaml template populated with customer-specific network and secret references.
  - Offline dependency list (OS packages, kernel requirements).

Customer requirements library (condensed checklist table):
- The customer requirements below are a minimal set to plan and validate a private deployment. For a full questionnaire, see Customer Requirements Form (link in related_pages).
  - Network: subnets (public/private), route tables, NAT gateways, firewall rules: PASSED/REVIEW
  - Identity: IAM roles, policies for node role, cross-account role for Redwood: PASSED/REVIEW
  - Secrets: KMS key ARN or HSM endpoint: PROVIDED
  - Storage: Encrypted block volumes, snapshot schedule: PROVIDED
  - Compute: GPU instance family (e.g., A100, H100), expected concurrent requests, batch sizes: PROVIDED
  - Compliance: Log retention window, data residency requirements, vulnerability scanning policy: PROVIDED

Day-2 operations (procedures, runbooks, and monitoring):
- Observability and SLOs:
  - Metrics to monitor (minimum): request latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, model cache hit rate, pod restart rate, node disk pressure, prometheus alerting rules.
  - SLOs: 99.5% availability for serving endpoints (per-customer SLA), P95 latency < configured SLO (customer-configurable, typical 150-300ms for 512-token requests).
  - Alert thresholds (examples): GPU utilization > 85% for 10m -> scale-up alert; node disk usage > 80% -> reclaim guidance.
- Backups and disaster recovery:
  - etcd/metadata backups: daily snapshot to S3 (or customer object storage) with 14-day retention (configurable).
  - Model cache: maintain signed model artifacts in registry; rebuild procedure described in runbook.
  - Playbook: data-plane node failure - steps to cordon, drain, reprovision nodes, and validate health.
- Capacity and scaling:
  - Horizontal autoscaling: recommended CPU/GPU node pool autoscaler configuration with safe scaling cooldowns (5-10 minutes).
  - Batching configuration: adjust continuous batching window based on P95 latency observed; use profiling tool to simulate production traffic.
- Common day-2 tasks (step-by-step):
  1. Validate cluster health: kubectl get nodes/pods, check Prometheus dashboards.
  2. Rotate credentials: follow secret rotation playbook (link to runbook).
  3. Apply resource quota changes: update node pool sizing via cloud console/terraform and monitor pod scheduling.

Upgrade and rollback procedures (prescriptive):
- Principles:
  - Always run upgrades in non-production environment first.
  - Prefer canary or blue/green strategies for control-plane upgrades.
  - Ensure automated backups and preflight checks complete before any upgrade.
- Upgrade checklist (control plane):
  1. Create a release branch and verify release manifests and image digests.
  2. Run preflight validation script: network checks, storage check, KMS access, and terraform drift detection.
  3. Take etcd/metadata snapshot and copy to a secure object store (retain at least 3 copies).
  4. Deploy control-plane upgrade to a canary namespace (5-10% of traffic) for 1-2 hours, monitor errors and latencies.
  5. If metrics are green, proceed to staged rollouts across remaining nodes with 10-20% increments.
  6. Post-upgrade validation: smoke test endpoints, run synthetic eval suite, confirm no regression in output quality.
- Rollback procedure (if severe regression or outage):
  1. Immediately stop rollout and redirect traffic to previous stable control plane or model variant (preconfigured fallback policy).
  2. Re-deploy previous release manifests using saved image digests.
  3. Restore etcd snapshot only if metadata indicates corruption (follow restore playbook; do not restore etcd for routine config rollbacks).
  4. Run full validation suite before resuming normal traffic.
  5. Postmortem and regression triage: capture traces, logs, and model evals to determine root cause.

Rollback examples and commands (illustrative):
- Snapshot etcd (Kubernetes example):
  - ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snapshot.db --endpoints=https://etcd-0:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/peer-ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/etcd/peer.key
  - aws s3 cp /tmp/etcd-snapshot.db s3://customer-backups/redwood/etcd/2027-07-15.db
- Rollback controller deployment to a pinned image digest:
  - kubectl set image deployment/redwood-controller controller=registry.redwood-inference.com/redwood-controller@sha256:<DIGEST> -n redwood-system
